done_when: forge work on a branch with an unfinished merge either hands the worker the conflicts to resolve and records its start without a partial commit (so the record lands with the merge commit), or, if that can't be done safely, refuses with a plain next step (resolve and commit the merge, then rerun) instead of a git error and a doctor hint; command tests cover a conflicted default-branch merge on a task and a fix, for a new repo and one adopted on an earlier release
why: forge work fails before the worker starts on a branch with a merge in progress ('git commit failed: fatal: cannot do a partial commit during a merge. Next: forge doctor'), because its 'is working' record is a partial commit; this traps branches whose default-branch merge left conflicts for a worker to resolve (reported by a client session on v1.2.8)
